Fanatics CEO: Sportsbook Marketing Could Hit $7B in 2027

Published October 19, 2026 · 4 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

Fanatics founder and CEO Michael Rubin told CNBC's Squawk Box that he expects the US sports betting industry's marketing spending to more than double next year, climbing from roughly $3 billion in 2025 to as much as $7 billion in 2027. Rubin's own company is planning for a similarly steep jump: he said Fanatics' marketing budget could rise from about $350 million this year to as much as $1 billion in 2027.

A distant third, but closing the gap

Rubin was candid about where Fanatics sits in the pecking order, calling it "a distant No. 3 in the betting and gaming business" behind FanDuel and DraftKings. Citing trailing-12-month CNBC figures, the article pegs US online sportsbook market share at roughly 34% for FanDuel, 31% for DraftKings, 8% for Hard Rock, 7% for BetMGM, and 6% for Fanatics — though Rubin separately described his company as "approaching 10%," a figure that doesn't fully square with the 6% cited elsewhere in the same report.

Why the marketing math is changing

The forecast comes as the two market leaders face a tougher stretch on Wall Street: DraftKings shares are down roughly 48% year-to-date, and Flutter Entertainment, FanDuel's parent, is down roughly 65%. Rubin pointed to rising competition from prediction market platforms as a factor squeezing the traditional sportsbook business, predicting the next couple of years "won't be a fun" period for the sector, with more competitive pressure but little consolidation expected among the largest operators.

On the product side, Rubin said Fanatics is expanding its Fair Play injury-protection feature to cover qualifying NFL and NBA bets when a player is injured at any point in the game, not just before halftime as under the prior rule. He also said Fanatics expects to issue roughly $2 billion in FanCash loyalty credit next year, with 97% to 98% typically redeemed within 12 months.

A rising marketing-spend forecast from an operator's own CEO is a prediction, not a commitment — actual 2027 budgets will depend on how the prediction-market competition and the broader betting market play out over the next several months.

What it means for bettors

Heavier marketing spending usually shows up to bettors as more sign-up offers, odds boosts, and loyalty perks as operators compete harder for market share — but it doesn't change the underlying math of any individual bet. If the forecast holds, expect a louder promotional environment heading into 2027 across the major sportsbook apps; see our sports betting guides for how to evaluate any offer on its actual terms rather than its size.
